name: ICM-20689 Accelerometer/Gyroscope Sensor
description: The `icm20689` motion platform allows you to use your TDK InvenSense ICM-20689 Accelerometer/Gyroscope sensors with ESPHome. The [SPI Bus](https://esphome.io/components/spi/) is required to be set up in your configuration for this sensor to work.

config_entries.label: Update Interval
config_entries.description: The interval at which sensor data is read. Defaults to `250ms`.

config_entries.label: CS Pin
config_entries.description: The CS pin of the sensor.

config_entries.label: Mode
config_entries.description: Pin mode flags (input / output / pullup / pulldown / open_drain). Combine flags as needed — e.g. input + pullup for a button pulled to VCC.

config_entries.label: Open Drain
config_entries.description: Set the open drain mode flag.

config_entries.label: Inverted
config_entries.description: Invert the logical level. ``true`` swaps high/low in software so an active-low button reads as active when grounded.

config_entries.label: Accelerometer Range
config_entries.description: The full-scale range of the accelerometer. One of `2G`, `4G`, `8G`, `16G`. Defaults to `2G`.

config_entries.label: Axis Map
config_entries.description: Remap or invert the physical axes of the sensor to match your board orientation. Each key (`x`, `y`, `z`) maps to the physical axis it should read from, optionally prefixed with `-` to invert. All three axes must be present and each physical axis may only appear once. Mutually exclusive with `transform_matrix`.

config_entries.label: Gyroscope Range
config_entries.description: The full-scale range of the gyroscope. One of `250DPS`, `500DPS`, `1000DPS`, `2000DPS`. Defaults to `250DPS`.

config_entries.label: Transform Matrix
config_entries.description: A 3×3 transformation matrix applied to raw accelerometer and gyroscope readings. This allows arbitrary calibration beyond simple axis remapping. Can be specified as a flat list of 9 values (row-major order) or as a 3×3 nested list. Mutually exclusive with `axis_map`. The matrix can be obtained from the runtime calibration actions described below — after calibration the computed matrix is logged in a format that can be copied directly into your configuration for persistent use.
